clue.text: Campaign involves brute rejecting European advance

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the campaign word holds the other piece

parts.note: to press for something is to campaign for it

indicators.note: rejecting means the European letter is thrown out of the brute word

parts.note: an ogre is a brutish monster

explanation.surface: A political campaign is pushed forward by a thug who has turned his back on Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress as a verb or noun means moving forward, the same as advance.

clue.text: Fair leader of Tories in charge

indicators.note: in means the first letter of the party name sits inside the charge word

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A summer fair is run by the head of the local Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, typically a village fundraising event with stalls and games.

clue.text: Flash character purchasing hot material

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in or acquiring, so the outer pieces hold the hot letter

parts.note: a mo, as in 'half a mo', is a moment or flash
an air is a manner or character, as in 'an air of mystery'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A flashy person shops for a fabric that is in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like a showy person, but here it means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a yarn or fabric made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Nice cop with info runs in woman

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: in means the runs letter is placed inside the woman word

parts.note: a dame is a woman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pleasant policeman has information about a woman who has been running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like an adjective, but it is the French city, so the definition means a French policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer, the kind found in the city of Nice.

clue.text: Radio One declined in series on unfinished collection

indicators.note: declined means sank lower, so in this down clue the one letter drops to the bottom of the word

parts.note: trains are series, as in a train of thought
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: unfinished means the collection word loses its last letter

parts.note: a store is a collection or stock

explanation.surface: A radio station's number one track has slipped in the charts during a run of a half-finished compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declined' moves the I in TRAINS down to the end, making TRANSI; 'on' puts it above STOR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor, short for transistor radio, is a small portable radio set.

clue.text: Extremes of uneven sea, fearsome and perilous

indicators.note: the extremes of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rough, frightening sea is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsafe and perilous are synonyms, both describing something dangerous.

clue.text: Gory, reportedly swelled a little

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to have grown a bit is to have 'grew some'

explanation.surface: A gory story, which we hear has grown a bit in the telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome and gory both describe something horrific, especially full of blood.

clue.text: Almost damn sweetheart supporting former partner's alibi

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the damn word is dropped

parts.note: to cuss is to swear or damn
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone nearly curses a lover who is backing up an ex-partner's story.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse is a reason offered in defence, the role an alibi plays.

clue.text: Making a slip chopping head off fish

indicators.note: chopping the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles while beheading a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means going wrong, so it equals making a slip or mistake.

clue.text: Start to openly gaze and lecherously eye

definitions.text: Start to openly gaze and lecherously eye

indicators.note: the start to each word is its first letter, taken from all four words

explanation.surface: A man begins by staring openly and then eyes someone up lecherously.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the first letters spell the answer, and the clue describes doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with obvious sexual desire.

clue.text: Unwitting detectives interrupt a copper facing gangster

indicators.note: facing means the pieces stand side by side, one before the other
to interrupt is to break in, so the detectives go inside the coin word

parts.note: a cent is a copper coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives
Al Capone was the famous gangster

explanation.surface: Police detectives unknowingly disturb a policeman confronting a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Accidental means happening without intent, so an accidental act is unwitting.

clue.text: Drunk, audibly lairy, occasionally finding drink

indicators.note: audibly means the word is heard, not read, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: necked is slang for drunk or swallowed quickly, as in necked a pint

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rowdy drunk at times finds something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lairy' is British slang for loud and aggressive; its alternate letters give A and R. 'Drunk' looks like a description of a person, but it is the past tense of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods in Greek myth, and any delicious drink.

clue.text: Explore excavation obtaining nearly every gem

parts.note: to tour is to travel round and explore

indicators.note: obtaining means getting hold of, so the excavation word holds the other piece

parts.note: a mine is an excavation

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: all and every both mean the whole of a group

explanation.surface: A tour of a dig turns up almost every gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline mineral cut as a gemstone in many colours.

clue.text: Endlessly tough holding falling water with this?

definitions.text: Endlessly tough holding falling water with this?

indicators.note: holding means the shortened tough word contains the water word
endlessly means the last letter of the tough word is lost

parts.note: stern means tough or severe
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A firm sieve holds back falling water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a sieve holds food back while the water falls through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer is a sieve or colander, used to drain water away from food.

clue.text: Low-down run taking victory over a run

indicators.note: taking means the victory letter is brought in
over means taking over the place of one run letter

parts.note: to scurry is to run hurriedly
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: A sneaky run that earns a win from a single run in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: SCURRY has two Rs; only one is replaced, which gives SCURVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy as an adjective means mean, contemptible and low-down, as in a scurvy trick.

clue.text: Shifting sound keeps artist up

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the sound word holds the reversed artist

parts.note: viable means sound or workable, as in a sound plan

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A changing noise keeps the painter awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise but means workable.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable means liable to change, so it describes something shifting.

clue.text: The man twice caught admitting sex over fast?

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the two caught letters hold the reversed sex word
twice means the caught letter is given two times

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A man twice caught having sex rushes things.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is loose: a hectic day is busy, not literally fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means frantic and rushed, with things happening at a fast pace.

clue.text: Flower circle Matisse describes

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw it round, so the answer is drawn from inside the words

explanation.surface: A flower painted by Matisse in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts inside 'circle', at its second C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant with large showy flowers.

clue.text: Handle revolutionary end to raucous parties

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the handle word reads backwards

parts.note: a lever is a handle

indicators.note: the end to a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Coping with a revolutionary who puts an end to rowdy parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb, but it is a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are lively parties and celebrations, a plural noun just like parties.

clue.text: Drive around two miles in traffic

indicators.note: around means the drive word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to drive someone to do something is to coerce them

indicators.note: two means the miles letter appears twice

explanation.surface: A two-mile drive through traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like vehicles, but it means trade, as in the drug traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun means trade or dealing in goods, the same as commerce.

clue.text: Inside shop a queue's becoming dense

indicators.note: inside means the answer is found within the letters of the words

explanation.surface: Inside a shop, the queue is getting packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means impossible to see through, and figuratively hard to understand or dim, both senses of dense.

clue.text: Informed of Republican in weakened case

indicators.note: in means the Republican letter goes inside the weakened word
case means the weakened word is the outer shell round it

parts.note: waned means grew weaker

explanation.surface: Told about a Republican in a feeble legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Warned means told of a danger in advance, a past form of informed.

clue.text: Suspicious about townie on vacation getting tasteless

indicators.note: about means the suspicious word goes round the other piece

parts.note: wary means cautious or suspicious

indicators.note: on vacation means empty, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: A suspicious city type on holiday finds the food bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery food or drink is thin and weak, so it lacks flavour.

clue.text: Cause to contain mass upset rejected in House

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the cause word holds the other piece

parts.note: a parent is a cause or origin, as in the parent of an idea

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or upset

explanation.surface: A political cause holds a large protest that is thrown out of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MAIL round to make LIAM, which goes inside PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A House, as in the House of Commons, is a chamber of a national legislature.

clue.text: Paddle round top of ocean?

indicators.note: round means the paddle word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a bat, as in table tennis, is a paddle

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rowing around on the surface of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a craft you paddle round on the ocean's surface, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a vessel that travels on water, often propelled by a paddle.

clue.text: Disgrace of guts turning in bar

indicators.note: the guts of the bar word are its middle pair, and turning them in it swaps their order

parts.note: a bolt is a bar that slides to lock a door

explanation.surface: A disgraceful scene of someone's stomach churning in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the bolt on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain on someone's reputation, a disgrace.

clue.text: The French crazy about taking new subway?

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the reversed pieces hold the new letter
about means turned around, so the two pieces read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: Frenchmen are mad about the new underground railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LENUT into TUNEL, and N goes in the middle. Subway is the British word for a pedestrian underpass, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel is an underground passage, and a subway in Britain is a pedestrian underpass.

clue.text: Scornful of sound including Queen in publicity

indicators.note: including means the sound word holds the other pieces

parts.note: sonic means relating to sound

indicators.note: in means the Queen letter goes inside the publicity word

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Mocking the noise when the Queen appears in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking, a synonym of scornful.
